summary: AgriCycle is a decision-support tool for farmers. It answers one question: what should I plant next? The farmer marks the field on a map and enters irrigation water, the current rotation, soil type and ranked priorities. AgriCycle then compares three 2–4 year crop rotations with the farmer’s own rotation, based on irrigation need, months the soil stays covered, erosion, and estimated net return. It also replays real dry or hot years from the field’s own NASA climate record to show how each rotation would hold up. This addresses the Field Shift challenge: it helps farms adapt to changing seasons with NASA data, shows the trade-offs and uncertainty openly, and supports local expertise without replacing it.
details:
The farmer moves through eight screens: Farm map → Farm setup → Farm diagnosis → Recommendations → Build your own → Financial analysis → Erosion map → Hard year. The tool works in Arabic and English.

• Water: crop water need from FAO-56 (ETc = Kc × ET0, Hargreaves ET0) with a daily soil-water balance. Irrigation shortfall = needed − available.

• Soil: rotation rules for legumes, cereal-after-cereal and bare fallow, plus months of soil cover. Erosion uses RUSLE on 30 m cells inside the field.

• Income: revenue minus seed, fertilizer, labour, other costs and water, in ₪. The farmer can replace prices, yields and costs with their own numbers.

• Ranking: each criterion is scored 1–5, then weighted by the farmer’s priorities into a 0–100 suitability score. All rotations use the same data and assumptions.

• Hard Year Test: applies a recorded dry or hot year to every year of the rotation, showing shortfall, heat and frost at flowering, and ranking changes.

• Rainfall outlook: a logistic regression for Nov–Apr below-normal rain, tested on unseen seasons against the 33% climatology baseline. The app says openly when it doesn’t beat the baseline.

• Tools: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn), FastAPI, Leaflet, vanilla JavaScript/HTML/CSS.

• Goal: help farmers see the trade-offs between water, soil and income before committing to a planting plan.

Use of SI or NASA Data

• NASA POWER: daily rainfall and temperature since 1981, used for crop water need, risk scores and the hard-year record.

• NASA SRTM (30 m): slope for the erosion map and field terrain.

• MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI (via ORNL DAAC): crop cycles and months when the land is bare.

• GPM IMERG: monthly correction of POWER rainfall to local levels (1998–2025).

• SI / ML: a logistic regression for the seasonal rain outlook, compared with the historical baseline using the Brier score and 300 bootstrap refits for uncertainty.

• NASA POWER API: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/

• NASA SRTMGL1 30 m; NASA Earthdata (GPM IMERG): https://earthdata.nasa.gov/

• MODIS MOD13Q1 via ORNL DAAC: https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/1600; NASA GIBS
